title: Hazard Pay: a top-down horde ARPG I'm building with Claude Opus 5.5, Tripo3D, Blender MCP, Nano Banana, ElevenLabs and Godot (trailer + what I've learned)
author: ohsoentitled
selftext:
Hazard Pay (working title) is a top-down horde ARPG. You're a contractor for a mining corporation, driving armed mining vehicles through alien swarms on a planet the company would rather you didn't ask questions about. You mine ore, survive the horde, fit out your vehicles and slowly work your way up the corporate ladder. Everything in it was captured in-engine. I’d love a bit of feedback but I’m also here to share a bit about how it’s been built so far.

**The stack**

**Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code):** writes basically all the code, the data, the shaders and the tooling scripts, and drives every other tool on this list.

**Godot 4.7:** typed GDScript only, with all content (vehicles, modules, enemies, quests, sounds) as JSON validated against schemas.

**Tripo3D:** image-to-3D for the alien creatures and vehicles.

**Blender + MCP / Blender Python:** props, buildings, environment kits, plus rigging and animating the Tripo models.

**Nano Banana:** concept art, loading screens, codex illustrations, item icons.

**ElevenLabs:** radio voices, sound effects and music, including the combat track in the trailer.

**Remotion:** the trailer itself was cut in code. Claude scripted the captures with Godot's Movie Maker, then built the edit, captions and music sync in React.

**Some things I’ve learned**

Blender MCP is great for hard-surface assets. Tripo3D is far better for anything organic. I had Claude use Nano Banana to generate concept art from the front and side and then used Tripo’s multi view images to 3D flow to get pretty high quality assets for aliens. 

Calling Nano Banana from Claude was a huge time saver. I was previously using Gemini and then importing images into Claude or Tripo3D but found I could just give Claude access to call via API keeping my workflow all in one place. 

I setup ElevenLabs the same way for voice acting. Claude calls via API and I added some skills there so that Claude is aware of how to add emphasis and emotion using ElevenLabs syntax. Initial attempts were quite emotionless and boring and I nearly gave up. 

On skills, I added some Godot skills which gave Claude a slightly better idea of how to architect the project well and utilize various features of Godot well for optimal performance.

comments.author: Timely-Tradition-471
comments.body:
Really interesting to see how you’ve divided the workflow between the different tools, especially using multi-view images to build out the alien creatures. It sounds like you’ve put a lot of thought into making the whole pipeline work together, from asset creation to animation and even cutting the trailer in code. I’d be interested to see how the final game is coming together.

I’m Josh, part of the Tripo Studio team on the U.S. side. I’d love to connect and learn more about the project and your experience using Tripo for organic assets. What kind of game are you building, and are you already using these assets in a playable build?
